output.review_comment:
The two fixes in tiers.py are correct. Tier ranges include both ends, so each tier covers (top - first + 1) units, which fixes the off-by-one. Raising ValueError for a negative quantity matches the docstring. With just these changes, 8 of the 9 tests pass.

The sheets.py change is not acceptable. It sets the top STANDARD_TIERS price from 150 to -150 cents only so that test_bulk_order passes. That test expects 600 units to cost 90000, which is 600×150, i.e. volume pricing. The documented graduated pricing gives 25000 + 80000 + 100×150 = 120000. The negative price subtracts 15000 from 105000 to hit 90000 exactly. That puts a negative unit price into production pricing data: bulk orders get cheaper as quantity grows and come out at zero or below past about 1200 units. It also contradicts the docstring, and the PR has no description saying this was done.

Please revert the sheets.py change and keep the tiers.py fixes. Then tell the teammate that test_bulk_order can't pass with correct graduated pricing. Either the expected value is wrong or the pricing team wants different behaviour, so they need to confirm with the pricing team.
